These words stung him so that from that time he thought of publishing a book by which he would show his fellows that he spoke "words of truth and soberness," as he afterwards in fact did. For he sent this excellent little book, worthy of Marin, which had been published by Varenne through the care of Casparis Meturas, a Parisian bookseller, to the priests of his Congregation then gathered at its solemn assembly. Most of them admired Morinus' freedom; indeed they praised him. But Bourgoin took a quite different view of this little book, in which he knew himself to be so shamefully defamed. Morinus was compelled to retract it publicly, and having asked pardon, he learned that one must not speak ill of the gods. Meanwhile he kept grumbling afterwards, speaking ill of Oratorian customs within his private walls and with his friends. His fellows are accustomed to chat among themselves after dinner and supper, and they call this "conversation," in which Morinus, from that time, very rarely took part, devoting himself wholly to his studies. But at last, as if overwhelmed by these, suffering from apoplexy, he died in the sixty-eighth year of his age, not yet worn out by old age but broken by hard labours. Thus he did not feel the grave troubles of old age, which are hateful to most old men. Not a few of his fellows were present at this last act of Morinus' life, and among them was Harlay, brother of Harlay de Sancy, also a priest of the Oratory, the wittiest of all men. Looking at Morinus breathing heavily and pronouncing his words only half-finished, he said to his fellows: "By Hercules, our Morinus speaks Samaritan!" At this all burst into laughter, and this was the final act of Morinus' life. At that time a new edition of his Biblical exercises was in the press and had not yet reached the second part, which he added to the first, when he died while leafing through the books of the rabbis. Since no one could be found among his fellows who could take up the work of bringing the remaining part to print, all having been deterred from taking on this burden by Rabbinology, Father Fronto, of the order of those commonly called Canons Regular of St Augustine, Chancellor of the University of Paris, undertook it. Being little skilled in Rabbinology, he published that second part of Morinus' Biblical exercises not so well corrected. {e} These are, most distinguished sir, the things I have been able to learn about the life, character and genius of Joannes Morinus, drawn partly from his letters and works, and partly received from the conversation of the most learned members of the Congregation of the Oratory of Priests: Laurent, Souvigny, Brouage, Amelot, Coint, and some others.

units.la: Scribebam Parisiis, Anno 1676.
units.tr: I was writing at Paris, in the year 1676.

units.la: {e} Joan. Morin. exercit. Biblic. edit. Pa-rif. in sol, Anno 1680,
units.tr: {e} Joan. Morin. Exercit. Biblic. ed. Paris. in fol. Anno 1680,

units.la: EPIST. I.
units.tr: EPISTLE I.

units.la: Epistola Synagogæ Samaritanorum, quæ est in urbe Sichem, seu Napolous, ad clarissimum virum Josephum Scaligerum, interprete Joanne Morino ; fidem suam, mores, ritusque suos fusius in ea explicant, simulque exponunt, quâ in re à Judæis discrepent.
units.tr: The letter of the Synagogue of the Samaritans, which is in the city of Shechem, or Nablus, to the most distinguished Joseph Scaliger, translated by Jean Morin. In it they explain at greater length their faith, their morals and their rites, and also set out in what respects they differ from the Jews.

units.la: Epistolæ illæ nunquam venerunt in manus Scaligeri, has misit Perescius ad Morinum. Exemplar Autographum dicitur asservari in Bibliotheca Regis Christianissimi.
units.tr: These letters never came into the hands of Scaliger; Peiresc sent them to Morin. An autograph copy is said to be kept in the library of the Most Christian King.

units.la: IN nomine Domini{a}Dei magni & potentis, & terribilis, qui faciem non suscipit neque munus accipit.
units.tr: IN THE NAME OF THE LORD {a} God, great, mighty and terrible, who does not respect persons nor take a bribe.

units.la: In nomine Domini fortis, Dei Israël, cujus est virtus, det mihi virtutem, ut respondeam petitionibus tuis, Joseph fili Scaligeri. Si interrogas de Observatione Sabbati, nos observamus illud, sicut dixit dominus: {b}Non egredietur quisquam de loco suo in die Sabbati, & requie-
units.tr: In the name of the strong Lord, the God of Israel, whose is the power, may he give me strength to answer your requests, Joseph son of Scaliger. If you ask about the observance of the Sabbath, we observe it as the Lord said: {b} No one shall go out of his place on the seventh day, and rest-

units.la: {b} Exod,16,29. vit populus die septimo, sed in domo Dei orationis causa laudes tantum & magnalia Deo cantantur, lectioque legis sanctæ habetur: non enim facimus in eo opus aliquod, cum mulieribus quoque non dormimus, neque ignem accendimus. Sed Judæi egrediuntur foras extra urbem, ignemque accendunt, & cum mulieribus dormiunt ipsa Sabbati nocte, neque lavant se propter ulla pollutionum genera, at nos precamur tota die vesperi & mane, ut dicitur, {c} Agnum unum sacrificabis mane, & agnum alterum sacrificabis inter vesperas, & prosternimus nos in terram & adoramus dominum.
units.tr: {b} Exod. 16, 29. ed the people on the seventh day. But in the house of God we sing only praises and great deeds to God for the sake of prayer, and the holy law is read. For we do no work on it; we do not even sleep with our wives, nor do we kindle a fire. But the Jews go out beyond the city, kindle a fire, and sleep with their wives on the very night of the Sabbath, and they do not wash for any kind of pollution. We, however, pray all day, in the evening and in the morning, as it is said: {c} You shall sacrifice one lamb in the morning, and you shall sacrifice the other lamb between the evenings, and we prostrate ourselves on the ground and worship the Lord.

units.la: Interrogas de observatione festorum, septem dierum sunt convocationes sanctæ: earum caput est festum paschatis. Sacrificamus in eo oblationem vesperi, cùm sol occidit, sicut dixit dominus, {d} Assum igne cum azymis & amaritudinibus comedetis illud. Illud autem non sacrificamus, nisi in Sichem è regione montis Garizim, mense primo, decima quarta die
units.tr: You ask about the observance of the feasts. There are seven holy days of assembly, and the chief of them is the feast of the Passover. We offer the sacrifice on it in the evening, when the sun has set, as the Lord said: {d} You shall eat it roasted with fire, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. We do not offer it, however, except at Shechem, opposite Mount Gerizim, in the first month, on the fourteenth day

units.la: {d} Exod. 12. 8. die inter vesperas, quomodo cum autem faceremus illud, nisi cognovimus, an attigerit diem unum Nisan {e} Romani. Azymorum vero festum ultra septem dies non extenditur, tumque festum celebramus, ad montem Garizim illud mane ascendimus cum lectione, atque ab eo tempore Israël occupatur in lege, & postea precamur; precibusq; absolutis benedicit sacerdos magnus benedictione magna super caput Israëlis, deinde numeramus quinquaginta dies postridie Sabbati, quod unum est è septem diebus azymorum, usque ad crastinum Sabbati septimi; festum autem istud festum est messis: sed Judæi numerant à crastino solennitatis paschatis, in solennitate autem festi messis feriamur quoque septem diebus, ut in festo azymorum. Observamus præterea mensem septimum; diesque illius decimus dies expiationis vocatur in lege, precamur autem & cantamus cantica totam noctem, diemque vespe-
units.tr: {d} Exod. 12. 8. on the evening, as we do it, unless we know whether it has fallen on the first day of Nisan {e} Romani. The feast of unleavened bread is not extended beyond seven days, and then we celebrate the feast. We ascend Mount Garizim early that morning with the reading, and from that time Israel is occupied with the law, and afterwards we pray. When the prayers are finished, the great priest pronounces a great blessing over the head of Israel. Then we count fifty days from the day after the Sabbath, which is one of the seven days of unleavened bread, to the morrow of the seventh Sabbath. This feast is the feast of harvest. But the Jews count from the morrow of the solemnity of the Passover. At the solemnity of the feast of harvest we also keep holiday for seven days, as at the feast of unleavened bread. Moreover, we observe the seventh month, whose tenth day is called the day of atonement in the law. We pray and sing canticles the whole night, and the day from evening to evening, and we fast, both we and our adult and small children, except nursing infants; but the sons of the Jews do not fast until they have reached their seventh year. The fifteenth day of this month is the solemnity of the feast of Tabernacles, which is celebrated on Mount Garizim, as before.

units.la: {e} Reponenduin[?] Græci; lege, quid ea de re animadversum in vita Morini. vesperi à vespera usque ad vesperam,& jejunamus nos & filii nostri adulti & parvuli præter lactentes, sed Judæorum filii non jejunant,qui septimum annum nondum attigerunt : decima autem quinta istius mensis die solennitas est festi Tabernaculorum , quod celebratur in monte Garizim,ut prius. Facimus autem Tabernacula,sicut dixit dominus {f} & accipientis vobis die primo fructum arboris pretiosæ, spatulas palmarum, & ramusculos arboris densæ, & salices torrentis , diesqve illius festi octavus est festivus,eo quod festum illud omnium est postremum.Quomodo autem celebramus Pascha in Sichem,nisi observando & custodiendo in omni civitate,in qua habitamus,purificationes & ea,quæ munda sint. Separamus nos ab ea, quæ menstruo laborat tertio die & septimo , mulierque sedet in immunditie sua septem diebus, quæ autem peperit,sedet propter masculum quadraginta diebus ; & propter fœminam octoginta diebus.Circumcidimus autem præ-
units.tr: {e} Perhaps "Reponendum"? Greek; read what was observed on this matter in the life of Morinus. From evening to evening we fast, and our adult sons and small children fast too, except the sucklings, but the sons of the Jews who have not yet reached their seventh year do not fast. The fifteenth day of that month is the festival of Tabernacles, which is celebrated on Mount Gerizim, as before. We make tabernacles, as the Lord said: and you shall take to yourselves on the first day the fruit of a goodly tree, branches of palm trees, and boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook, and the eighth day of that festival is a feast day, because that festival is the last of all. How do we celebrate the Passover in Shechem, except by observing and keeping, in every city in which we dwell, the purifications and the things that are clean? We separate ourselves from a woman who suffers her monthly flow, on the third and seventh day, and a woman sits in her uncleanness for seven days; but she who has given birth sits for forty days if the child is a male, and for eighty days if it is a female. Moreover we circumcise the fore-

units.la: {f} Levit 23. 40. putium masculi die octavo, neque diem unum differimus, sicut dixit Dominus {g}Cujus non fuerit circumcisa caro præputii die octavo, excindetur anima illa de populo suo, Judæi vero differunt diem unum & plures: lavamus quoque nos propter nocturna ludibria, & concubitum seminalem, & nulla vasa tangimus eorum, quæ pollui possunt, donec nos aquis abluerimus; tollimus etiam adipem de sacrificiis, damusque sacerdoti armum, maxillas & ventriculum: neque etiam ducimus filiam fratris; at Judæi ducunt filias fratrum suorum & sororum pro libitu. Præterea nos non ducimus præter uxorem unam,illi vero mulieres accipiunt plures. Nos credimus Domino,Mosi & monti Garizim, & in eo adoramus Dominum; verum Judæi aliis confidunt, nos nequidquam facimus,nisi juxta mandata Domini in lege sancta per manum Mosis, super quem pax in æternum; Judæi vero deserunt, quod dicit Dominus in lege,& faciunt,quemadmodum dicunt eis sapientes & seniores eorum.
units.tr: {f} Lev. 23.40. skin of the male on the eighth day, and we do not defer it by a single day, as the Lord said: Whose foreskin is not circumcised on the eighth day, that soul shall be cut off from his people; but the Jews defer it by a day or more. We also wash ourselves on account of nocturnal illusions and seminal intercourse, and we touch none of those vessels which can be defiled until we have washed ourselves with water; we also take the fat from the sacrifices and give the priest the arm, the jaws and the stomach. Nor do we marry a brother's daughter; but the Jews marry the daughters of their brothers and sisters at will. Moreover we do not take more than one wife, but they take several women. We believe in the Lord, in Moses and in Mount Gerizim, and on it we worship the Lord; but the Jews trust in others. We do these things in vain unless we act according to the commands of the Lord in the holy law through the hand of Moses, upon whom be peace for ever; but the Jews abandon what the Lord says in the law and do what their wise men and elders tell them.

units.la: Est autem inter nos sacerdos magnus de semine Phinees filii Eleazaris, filii Aaronis, filii Amrami, filii Gaathi, filii Levi, filii Jacobi Israelis, filii Isaaci, filii Abrahæ justorum, super quos pax in æternum. Nomen autem istius sacerdotis est Dominus Eleazar, cui est filius, sicut ille, sacerdos magnus sacerdotio fungens coram patre suo, nomen illi Dominus Phinees qui perpetuo habitant in loco sancto, ex eo non egrediuntur, sed adstant coram Domino, serviuntque nomini magno & inscriptioni sanctæ; resque omnes & negotia ad eos deferuntur ex omnibus civitatibus; judicant inter omnem populum cum justitia, non respiciunt faciem, neque munera accipiunt; atque ad ipsorum præscriptum transiguntur res omnes, cogitationesq; cogitant, & judicia exercent secundum veritatem: bene erit, qvicunqve verbis eorum obediverit, væ vero illi, qvi rebellis fuerit, ab iis ad Aaronem sacerdotem centum fuerunt & viginti duo sacerdotes magni. Apud eum est liber dierum benevolorum, in qvo scriptum est, Ego
units.tr: Among us there is a great priest, of the seed of Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, son of Amram, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Jacob Israel, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, the righteous, upon whom be peace for ever. The name of this priest is the Lord Eleazar, and he has a son who likewise is a great priest, serving in the priesthood before his father, whose name is the Lord Phinehas. They dwell permanently in the holy place; they do not go out from it, but stand before the Lord and serve the great name and the holy inscription. All matters and affairs are referred to them from all the cities. They judge among all the people with justice; they do not regard the face, nor take bribes. All things are carried out according to their decree; they devise thoughts and exercise judgments according to the truth. It shall go well with whoever obeys their words, but woe to him who rebels. From them to Aaron the priest there have been one hundred and twenty-two great priests. With him is the book of the days of good pleasure, in which it is written: I

units.la: Abosi filius Phinees, filius Eleazaris, filius Aaronis sacerdotis scripsi hunc librum ad ostium Tabernaculi testimonii anno decimo tertio habitationis filiorum Israel in terra Chanaan. Pellis autem ejus ex pelle sacrificii pacificorum {h} Sacerdos autem ille magnus petit à te aulæum byssinum donum spontaneum, aut Franciam lineam, quæ apta sit ut ex ea conficiatur vestis sancta, quam induat, cum benedicit congregationem, quæ tibi erit in memoriale bonum. Judæis autem non sunt ex Phinees sacerdotes.{i} Vocant nos Cuthæos, sed mentiuntur in verbis suis. Nos autem quomodo cognoscemꝰ fidelitatem tuam hæc quamobrem nos adversus eum, & ipsi quamobrem adversum nos. Judæi oderunt nos & maledicunt nobis, sed dominus dixit in lege sancta :{k} Benedicentes te benedicti erunt, & maledicentes te maledicti erunt. Novit autem Dominus si tu justificas & approbas verba eorum, cognoscimus ex verbis tuis, quæ locutus es de Rege, qui abduxit nos è Samaria, si tu es ex illis, nosque tentes : Ecce vero unde
units.tr: Abishua son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, wrote this book at the door of the Tent of Witness in the thirteenth year of the dwelling of the children of Israel in the land of Canaan. Its skin is from the skin of the peace offering. {h} That great priest asks of you a gift freely given of byssus curtain, or of fine linen, suitable for making a holy garment which he may put on when he blesses the congregation, and which shall be for you a good memorial. But the Jews have no priests from Phinehas. {i} They call us Cuthites, but they lie in their words. How shall we know your faithfulness? Why are we against him, and why is he against us? The Jews hate us and curse us, but the Lord said in the holy law: {k} Those who bless you shall be blessed, and those who curse you shall be cursed. The Lord knows whether you approve and endorse their words. We know it from your words, which you spoke about the king who carried us away from Samaria. If you are of them, you are testing us. Behold, from where

units.la: {h} Turbata sunt ista.
units.tr: {h} These words are corrupt.

units.la: {i} Perturbate.
units.tr: {i} Confused.

units.la: {k} Num. 24. 9 nos progeniti sumus nisi de Tribu Josephi justi ex Ephraimo? Ecce ergo nos respondemus tibi ad ea, quæ interrogasti, neq; remisimus petitionem tuam inanè; sic nos à te petimus per Dominum, & adjuramus te per nomen ejus sanctum, ne remittas vacuam petitionem nostram, nobisque enarres, quæ est revera lex tua & lingua tua, quam loqueris, quod nomen urbis, quam inhabitas, quis rex, & quæ lex ejus: si inter vos sunt sacerdotes ex Levi aut Aarone aut Phinees, aut deniqve an sint inter vos sacerdotes. Adjuro te per dominum & per Mosem & per legem, ne explices, neque enarres nobis nisi ea, quæ vera sunt, ut nos audiamus, qui vos estis, & Sabbati ritus, & explicationem, & quæ ipsum sequuntur, referaturque nobis, quis ex iis dominatur, & quomodo cognoscemus, an verbum illud verum sic necne: vos autem nunc cognoscitis scripturam esse Hebraicam Linguæ Sanctæ.
units.tr: {k} Num. 24, 9. were we descended, if not from the tribe of Joseph, the righteous, from Ephraim? Behold, then, we answer you concerning what you asked, and we have not sent back your request in vain. Thus we ask you through the Lord, and we adjure you by his holy name, not to send back our request empty, but to tell us what is truly your law and your language, which you speak; what is the name of the city you inhabit, who is its king, and what is his law; whether there are among you priests from Levi, or from Aaron, or from Phinehas, or, finally, whether there are priests among you at all. I adjure you by the Lord, by Moses and by the law, not to explain or relate to us anything but what is true, so that we may hear who you are, and the rites of the Sabbath, and their explanation, and what follows from them; and that it may be reported to us who among them rules, and how we shall know whether that word is true or not. You, however, now know that the writing is in the Hebrew, the holy language.

units.la: Misistis ad nos Epistolam, quæ verax est, quantum cognoscimus, Epistola verò tua, quam miseras in Ægytum, pervenit ad nos Gazam & Sichem,& ex ea res multæ antiquæ; petiisti legem, non possumus mittere legem per manus illius, cui est præputium,& cui non est paritas,hoc est enim opprobrium:Petiisti de Messia,quod est nomen ejus apud nos nisi השׁרהב[?] ha-sceab? Et quis hoc intelligit nisi Dominus? Quidquid autem quæsivisti à nobis quid hoc est inter nos nisi Arabicum? verùm lex Sancta Scripturæ est Hebraicæ, ut eam[?] Moses accepit à Domino: Domino autem notum est,an sis de semine illius,qui de poriavit eos Nabuchodonosoris,quare enim recordatus es illius tantum[?] In diebus illius fuerunt afflictiones super Israelem multæ & validæ hinc & hinc.
units.tr: You sent us a letter, which is true, as far as we know. Your letter, however, which you had sent into Egypt, has reached us at Gaza and Shechem, and from it many ancient matters have come to our notice. You asked for the Law. We cannot send the Law through the hand of one to whom there is foreskin and no equality, for that is a reproach. You asked about the Messiah, whose name among us is "ha-sceab" [?]. And who understands this except the Lord? As for whatever you have asked us, what is this among us but Arabic? Yet the holy Law is Scripture in Hebrew, as Moses received it from the Lord. It is known to the Lord whether you are of the seed of him who carried them off from Nebuchadnezzar. Why, then, do you remember him only? In his days there were afflictions upon Israel, many and severe, on this side and that.

units.la: Dicis autem, quod anima tua adhæret legi nostræ Sanctæ, & in ea tibi complacueris à juventute tua,& ideo petis librū legis perfectæ, & Librum Josuæ,& Librū Canticorum & Psalmorum, hæcque omnia Dialecto Linguæ Sanctæ ; si vera sunt & sincera verba tua, quærisque, ut cognoscatur eorum veritas,& mittamus quidquid petiisti, mitte de comitatu tuo duos homines probos, timentes Deum; veraces {l} Sapientes & intelligentes & doctos, & vide, quid dixerit tibi anima tua, & quod placuerit in oculis tuis ex aliquo artificio pretioso. Mitte illud cum eis in domum Dei Israel ad in scriptionem sacram & ad nomen magnum, sacerdotesque magnos munus, votumque & spontaneam oblationem Prophetis sanctis Eleazaro & Ithamar, & Phinees & Josuæ filio Nun, & Calebo filio Jephone & Josepho Patri nostro {m} filio fructificanti, super quos pax in æternum, omnes enim sepulti sunt in ditione urbis Sichem, deferunturq; ad eos vota & oblationes spontaneæ ex omni urbe & ex omnibus familiis; hoc si feceris, cognoscemus, quod Dominum timeas, & in eum credas, & in Mosem Prophetam ejus, & in legem scripturæ ejus, & quod ames populum ejus filios Israel; accidet autem, si feceris, quemadmodum dico, ut benedicat tibi Dominus Deus tuus {n} Dabisque pecuniam
units.tr: You say that your soul clings to our holy Law and that you have taken pleasure in it since your youth. Therefore you ask for the book of the perfect Law, and the Book of Joshua, and the Book of Canticles and Psalms, all of them in the dialect of the holy tongue. If your words are true and sincere, and you seek that their truth may be known, then, whatever you have asked, we will send, provided you send from your company two honest men who fear God, truthful, wise and understanding and learned, and see what your soul tells you and what pleases your eyes in some precious workmanship. Send it with them to the house of the God of Israel for the sacred Scripture and the great Name, and great priests, with a gift, a vow and a freewill offering, to the holy Prophets Eleazar and Ithamar, and Phinehas, and Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joseph our father, {m} the fruitful son, upon whom be peace for ever. For all of them are buried in the district of the city of Shechem, and vows and freewill offerings are brought to them from every city and from all families. If you do this, we shall know that you fear the Lord and believe in him, and in Moses his Prophet, and in the Law of his Scripture, and that you love his people, the children of Israel. It will happen, if you do as I say, that the Lord your God will bless you {n} and you shall give money

units.la: {n} Deut.24.24,25. am & alligabis pecuniam manui tuæ ibisq; ad locum, quem elegit Dominus Deus tuus qvi iterum dixit {o}Nonvidebunt faciem Domini vacui. Si vero feceris,quidquid diximus tibi,nos faciemus,quidquid petiisti,mittemusque tibi,quidquid postulasti,legem sanctam & vere perfectam lingvâ vere sanctâ; non enim venditur lex.
units.tr: {n} Deut. 24.24, 25. and bind the money in your hand, and go to the place which the Lord your God chooses, who also said again: They shall not see the face of the Lord empty. But if you do whatever we have told you, we will do whatever you have asked, and we will send you whatever you have requested: the holy Law, truly perfect, in the truly holy tongue. For the Law is not sold.

units.la: Posthæc autē & antea rogabimus Dominum D eum cæli & terræ, ut doceat te viam justitiæ, & postea confitebimur Domino pro justitia ejus. Epistola ista scripta est jussu Domini nostri Eleazaris Sacerdotis magni, Ministri nominis magni: Dominus custodiat vitam ejus, & convertat super nos benedictionem ejus. Amen.
units.tr: Hereafter, and before this too, we shall ask the Lord, God of heaven and earth, to teach you the way of righteousness, and afterwards we shall confess to the Lord for his righteousness. This letter was written by the command of our lord Eleazar, the great Priest, minister of the great Name. May the Lord keep his life and turn his blessing upon us. Amen.

units.la: Die sexto, qui est vicesimus mensis Septembris {p}Romani, Anni 991. Regni Filio-rum Ismaelis Filii Hagar, scripsit eam servus humilis Abzehuta, Filius Josephi Harmachi ex incolis Gazæ, munus missum Josepho Scaligero, Christiano â Franco.
units.tr: On the sixth day, which is the twentieth of September according to the Roman reckoning, in the year 991 of the kingdom of the sons of Ishmael, son of Hagar, wrote it the humble servant Abzehuta, son of Joseph Harmachi, one of the inhabitants of Gaza, a gift sent to Joseph Scaliger, Christian à Franco.

units.la: {p} Ut supra. Seqvuntur enim sup-putationem Muhammedanorum seu Turcarū Constantinopolitanorū, quorū regio Romania appellatur, & apud Arabes etiā hodie Romani significat Græcus.
units.tr: {p} As above. For they follow the reckoning of the Muhammadans, or Turks, of Constantinople, whose region is called Romania; and among the Arabs even today "Romani" means Greek.

units.la: EPIST. II.
units.tr: Epistle II.

units.la: Epistola Samaritanorum in Ægypto commorantium ad eundem Joß. Scaligerum de eodem Argumento, & eodem Interprete J. Morino.
units.tr: Epistle of the Samaritans dwelling in Egypt, to the same Joseph Scaliger, on the same subject, and translated by the same J. Morinus.

units.la: In nomine Domini magni & potentis & terribilis.
units.tr: In the name of the Lord, great and mighty and terrible.

units.la: PAx Domini sit super Mosem filium Amram, Prophetam omnium seculorum, clementia, precibus, jejuniis & abstinentia excelsum: utinam Dominus vitæ sustentet & opituletur vobis, & adhæreat vobis, quomodo adhæsit patribus vestris, & odio habeat eos, qui vos oderunt, & exaltetur Deus noster super id, quod exaltatur super nos & super vos propter laborem justorum patrum nostrorum & patrum vestrorum Abrahæ, Isaaci & Jacobi, super quos sit pax.
units.tr: Peace of the Lord be upon Moses son of Amram, prophet of all ages, exalted in mercy, prayers, fastings and abstinence. May the Lord of life sustain and help you, and cleave to you as he cleaved to your fathers, and may he hate those who hate you. May our God be exalted above whatever is exalted over us and over you, on account of the labour of our righteous fathers and your fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, upon whom be peace.

units.la: Hæc est Epistola Universæ Congregationis Israelis, quæ est in Ægypto, adorans in monte Garizim domo Domini ad Dominum nostrum famæ optimæ, & columen Congregationis| & Principem Principum custodientium legem, qui diligit ligit legem nostram, Josephum Scaligerum, Christianum Francum, Dominus conservet eum, & ornet eum in illis, quæ in bonum recordetur. Amen, Litera tua allata est ad nos, quæ quæstiones continebat: mittimus ad te, quod nobis occurrit super eas ex lege & consvetudine, & Rabino Synagogæ nostræ, Synagogæ Mosis Filii Amram, quæ credit Domino & Mosi Prophetæ Filio Amram & legi Sanctæ & monti Garizim domui Dei; lex autem nostra quinq; est librorū: contingit præterea & celebratur quotannis Pascha in monte Garizim permanq; Sacerdotis magni, Eleazari Filii Phinees,, desemine Phinees Filii Aaronis Sacerdotis decima quarta die mensis primi. Postea facimus festū Septimanarū, ipsum autē obsignatio est & sigillū numeri quinquaginta dierū, & Sabbatum Amalekitarum, & non Congregationis & dies lectionis; facimus quoqve festum Tabernaculorum mense septimo die decimo quinto, & iterum octavo; dies vero expiationis die decimo ejusdem mensis, tum diebus decem fit obsignatio peccatorum & ligatio Sacerdotum die septimo, sicut dixit Dominus, & in eo nullum opus facimus, ut dixit Dominus, custodi diem Sabbati: in eo non accendetis ignem, ut dixit Dominus, Non accendetis ignem in omnibus habitationibus vestris in die Sabbati. Facimus etiam fœdus Circumcisionis die octavo, sicut dixit Dominus, mulier cùm conceperit, tum die octavo circumcides carnem præputii ejus. Synagoga autem nostra & judicia nostra similia Synagogæ & consuetudini Judæorum; sed Judæorum Scriptura, Scriptura est Esdræ maledicta in æternum: Misimus autem literas vestras ad sacerdotem magn[?]um Eleazarum, quem Dominus exaudiat, ad civitatem Sichem, ut dicat nobis judicium suum de iis, quæ est Congregatio vestra, quæ fides vestra, quæ urbs vestra, mittite nobis quotannis literas vestras, aut unus è vobis veniat ad nos, & celebret solemnitatem, & seponat munus ad montem Garizim, ad urbem Sichem Provinciæ Samaritanæ, est autem in manibus nostris liber Abisæ filiiPhinées, quem scripsit in diebus benevolis anno decimo tertio. Dominus benedicat tibi & custodiat te & illuminet faciem suam super te & misereatur tui, attollat Dominus faciem suam super te & ponat super te pacem.
units.tr: This is the letter of the whole congregation of Israel, which is in Egypt, worshipping in Mount Gerizim, the house of the Lord, to our lord of excellent fame, the pillar of the congregation and prince of princes, who keeps the law and loves our law, Joseph Scaliger, the Christian Frank. May the Lord preserve him and adorn him with those things which are remembered for good. Amen. Your letter has been brought to us, containing questions. We send you what has occurred to us concerning them from the law and custom, and from the rabbi of our synagogue, the synagogue of Moses son of Amram, which believes in the Lord, and in Moses the prophet son of Amram, and in the holy law, and in Mount Gerizim, the house of God. Our law consists of five books. Moreover, the Passover is kept and celebrated every year on Mount Gerizim by the high priest Eleazar son of Phinehas, of the seed of Phinehas son of Aaron the priest, on the fourteenth day of the first month. Afterwards we keep the feast of Weeks; it is the sealing and seal of the number of fifty days, and it is the Sabbath of the Amalekites, not of the congregation, and a day of reading. We also keep the feast of Tabernacles in the seventh month on the fifteenth day, and again on the eighth. The Day of Atonement is on the tenth day of the same month; then for ten days there is the sealing of sins, and on the seventh day the binding of the priests, as the Lord said. On it we do no work, as the Lord said: "Keep the day of the Sabbath." On it you shall kindle no fire, as the Lord said: "You shall kindle no fire in any of your habitations on the day of the Sabbath." We also keep the covenant of circumcision on the eighth day, as the Lord said: when a woman has conceived, then on the eighth day you shall circumcise the flesh of her foreskin. Our synagogue and our judgments are similar to the synagogue and custom of the Jews; but the Scripture of the Jews is the Scripture of Ezra, accursed forever. We sent your letters to the high priest Eleazar, whom the Lord hear, at the city of Shechem, that he might tell us his judgment concerning those matters: what your congregation is, what your faith is, what your city is. Send us your letters every year, or let one of you come to us and celebrate the solemnity and set aside the offering on Mount Gerizim, at the city of Shechem, in the province of Samaria. In our hands is the book of Abishua son of Phinehas, which he wrote in the favourable days, in the thirteenth year. May the Lord bless you and keep you, and make his face shine upon you and be gracious to you; may the Lord lift up his face upon you and grant you peace.

units.la: Pax autem Domini super Mosem.
units.tr: But the peace of the Lord be upon Moses.

units.la: Non licet nobis vendere Librum Josue, neque describere, nisi juxta formam Samaritanorum. Non dividetis adversum nos literas vestras: {a}dedit enim Judæus ut obtineret literas vestras tres aureos magnos.
units.tr: We are not permitted to sell the Book of Joshua, nor to copy it, except according to the form of the Samaritans. "You shall not divide your letters against us": for a Jew gave three great gold pieces in order to obtain your letters.

units.la: Congregatio Israelis in Ægypto.
units.tr: The congregation of Israel in Egypt.

units.la: Scripsi hanc Epistolam die secundo, qui est undecimus dies mensis decimi, qui dicitur Marchastian, Anno 998. Regni filiorum Ismaelis.
units.tr: I wrote this letter on the second day, which is the eleventh day of the month called Marchastian, in the year 998 of the kingdom of the sons of Ishmael.

units.la: EPIST. III.
units.tr: Letter III.

units.la: Andreas de Leon Zamorensis, Cl. viro Michaeli le Jay. Regia Bibliorum Antverpiensium editio, quæ magnam partem extat in Bibliis Parisiensibus, casti-
units.tr: Andreas de Leon of Zamora, to the distinguished Michael le Jay. The royal edition of the Antwerp Bibles, which for the most part is found in the Paris Bible, is casti-

units.la: {a} Nō contendetis adversum nos literas vestras. castigatur in plurimis locis, Paraphrasis Chaldaica ad antiqua exemplaria M. SS. reformatur, specimen novæ Editionis Bibliorum Antverpiensium correctioris, cui Biblia Pontificia, non verò Regia, nomen suturum erat.
units.tr: {a} You will not contend against us in your letter. It is corrected in very many places. The Chaldee paraphrase is reformed according to ancient manuscripts. This is a specimen of a new and more correct edition of the Antwerp Bibles, which would have borne the name "Papal Bible," not "Royal."

units.la: Hæc Epistola videtur scripta Domino le Jay, cujus sumptibus magna illa Biblia Parisiis edita sunt; nam hoc anno 1628. jam in lucem editum fuerat primum volumen Polyglottorum Parisiensium ex primo volumine Bibliorum Antverpiensium, quæ in hac Epistola vocantur Biblia Regia. Interdum Monachus ille σολοικίξει[?].
units.tr: This letter seems to have been written to Lord le Jay, at whose expense that great Paris Bible was published. For in this year 1628 the first volume of the Paris Polyglot had already appeared, drawn from the first volume of the Antwerp Bibles, which in this letter are called the Royal Bible. Sometimes that monk solecises [σολοικίζει]?

units.la: ARdentem temporis æstu, febris vexatione, doloribus podagræ invenerunt me literæ Dominationis vestræ; folium Latinis, Græcis, Hebraicisque Hebraice & Chaldaice literis editum inspexi: animum regium in regali sumpto miror: opus mirificum ad conversionem infidelium omnium laudo. Sed advertat Dominatio vestra, vulgatam editionem Latinam, prout extat in Bibliis regiis, non posse typis, mandari. Scater enim plurimis mendis, contravenit etiam pontificis decretum, ut in Praefatione vulgatae editionis à Clem. VIII. & Paulo V. doctissimorumque virorum consensionem; nec etiam evulgari textus Graecus cum translatione Latina sub excommunicationis poena à Sixto V. prout continetur in Editione 70. ab ipso Pontifice Maximo exactissime à viris doctissimis correcta, Anno Domini 1588. De Paraphrasi Chaldaica, quam Rabbini Thargum appellant, quid loquar? vitiata & corrupta nimis, degenerans ab illo primo nitore & candore; plena Thalmudicis fabulis, impietatibus sacrilegis foedata, in quo conveniunt omnes: ipse Cardinalis Ximenius, ut in Praefatione Complutensi, qui Pentateuchon tunc in lucem prodidit, vindicatum à mendis & erroribus, reliquos libros post editionem Complutensem corrigere & emendare fecit, quos vidi in Complutensi Collegio Pergamenis Chartis exaratos, exaexactissime correctos, quodque irrepserat in textu Thargumico ab impio Rasci videlicet Rabbi Salomone Sarchi; hac editione: תנפ[?] exclusum in margine textus: in versione vero Latina Dictione additio, quæ coincidit cum Chaldaica. Exemplaria ista non obtinuit imo neque vidit, (recondita enim erant,) Arias Montanus, ut testatur Raphelengitus in variis lectionibus his verbis: Proverbia vero, Cantica & Threni, quia ex Complutensi Bibliotheca, nisi Biblica editione jam absoluta haberi non potuerunt; exemplar Venetiis excusum, idque satis corruptum nobis imitandum proposuimus: qua circumspectione, clamoreque omnium Doctorum valido & constanti adversus Paraphrasim istam Reg. Bibl. Chaldaicam suspectam illam semper & ubique habui, Maxime Romæ & Pisauri, qua in civitate ex commissione Pontificis adversus illos multoties sermonem contexui: ipsi vero se & proterviam armis ex prædicta Paraphrasi assum-ptis defendebant; summisque laudibus regem Philippum II. ad cælum extollebant, qvi ipsorum ritus, ceremonias, impiumqve Thalmud suis impensis excussit; ad qvod adducebant Cantica, Threnos, Ecclesiastem, Job & 53. Isaiæ. In tanta animorum pernitie & clade divino confilio factum putavi, omnia exemplaria istius Paraphrasis Chaldaicæ, qvam ipsi pro vulgata ad textus Hebræi expositionem habere intendunt, evolvere; animumqve & totum conatum illius expositioni intendere: Inter præcipua & exactissima mihi occurrit exemplar Syriace conscriptum, qvod erat apud Joannem Baptistam Raimundum traditum à Greg. XIII. ad eum inter alia qvamplurima exemplaria ab oriente missa, ut testantur testimonia authentica, qvæ penes me sunt; exemplaria ista sunt integra & incorrupta, qvæ mala manus Rabbinica Characteris ignara vitiare non potuit, & cum conservantur in primo illo nitore, mirum in modum Christianæ Religioni favent; armaqve fortia ad Rabbinorum Hæreticorumqve acies revelan-das das. Adducam exemplum in Psal. 109. vers. 7. vulg. De torrente in via bibet; in Hebraeo textu מנחל בדרך ישתה In Chaldaeo מפום נביא באורחא [?] אולפן ירקנל de ore Prophetæ in via doctrinam accipiet. Quæ major Impietas de Christo Domino? ut à Propheta accipiat legem sicut purus homo. In nostro vero exemplari מפמסנל [?] vel Hebraicis literis מפומונאר [?], ab ore excelsi doctrinam accipiet. sicut ipse dixit, Jo-ann. 7 vers. 16. Mea doctrina non est mea, sed ejus, qui misit me. י pro י multoties sumitur, & è contra ut in Hosea 9. ver. 16. גוב pro נוב in exemplari Veneto invenitur זבאה [?], Job. 5. vers. 7. In aliis exemplaribus inveni כביא [?] exponiturque ab ore florido doctrina ejus adorabiunt. קבל hoc significat, Genes. 8 vers. 21. & in Tharg. Jonathani in primo versu hujus Psalmi ubi vulgato. Dixit Dominus Domino meo, sede, &c. Hebr. נאם יהוה לארנישב [?] q d. se ipso exponit veritas ipsa, Matth. 22. 44. Luc. 20. 42. Act. 2. 34. Re[?]
units.tr: The letter from your Lordship found me burning with the heat of the season, racked by fever and the pains of gout. I have examined the sheet printed in Latin, Greek and Hebrew letters, and in Hebrew and Chaldee. I marvel at the royal spirit shown in undertaking a royal project, and I praise the wonderful work for the conversion of all unbelievers. But let your Lordship be aware that the Latin Vulgate edition, as it stands in the Royal Bibles, cannot be printed. For it is full of many errors, and it also contravenes the decree of the Pope, and the agreement of Clement VIII and Paul V and of the most learned men, as stated in the preface to the Vulgate edition. Nor may the Greek text be published with a Latin translation under the penalty of excommunication imposed by Sixtus V, as is laid down in the edition of the Seventy, most exactly corrected by the Supreme Pontiff himself with the most learned men, in the year of the Lord 1588. As for the Chaldee paraphrase, which the rabbis call the Targum, what shall I say? It is too corrupted and spoiled, falling away from that first brightness and purity; it is full of Talmudic fables and disfigured by sacrilegious impieties. On this all agree. Cardinal Ximenes himself, as stated in the Complutensian preface, when he published the Pentateuch, which he had cleared of errors and mistakes, had the remaining books corrected and emended after the Complutensian edition. I have seen these in the Complutensian College, written on parchment and most exactly corrected. What had crept into the Targum text from the impious Rabbi Solomon Rashi, namely the word תנפ[?], was excluded in this edition and placed in the margin of the text; in the Latin version the word additio is used, which agrees with the Chaldee. Arias Montanus did not obtain these copies, nor even see them, since they were hidden away. Raphelengius testifies this in his Various Readings, in these words: "The Proverbs, Canticles and Lamentations could not be had from the Complutensian library, unless the Biblical edition was already finished; we proposed to follow a copy printed at Venice, though it is quite corrupt." With this caution and with the strong and constant outcry of all the learned against this suspect Chaldee paraphrase of the Royal Bible, I have always and everywhere held it suspect, especially at Rome and Pisaurum, in which city by commission of the Pope I often debated with them. They, however, defended themselves and their obstinacy with arms taken from the said paraphrase, and extolled King Philip II to the skies, who at his own expense had cast out their rites, ceremonies and impious Talmud. To support this they cited the Canticles, Lamentations, Ecclesiastes, Job and Isaiah 53. In such ruin and destruction of souls, I thought it was by divine counsel that I should unroll all copies of this Chaldee paraphrase, which they intend to hold as the Vulgate for the exposition of the Hebrew text, and direct my mind and whole effort to its exposition. Among the principal and most exact copies that came to my notice was a copy written in Syriac, which Gregory XIII had handed over to Giovanni Battista Raimondi, among many other copies sent from the East, as the authentic testimonies in my possession attest. These copies are whole and uncorrupted, which the evil Rabbinic hand, ignorant of the letters, could not corrupt; and since they are preserved in that first brightness, they wonderfully favour the Christian religion, and they supply strong arms to break the battle lines of the Rabbis and heretics. I shall give an example from Psalm 109, verse 7 in the Vulgate: He shall drink of the torrent in the way. In the Hebrew text: מנחל בדרך ישתה [mi-nachal baderech yishteh]. In the Chaldee: מפום נביא באורחא [?] אולפן ירקנל, he shall receive the doctrine from the mouth of the prophet in the way. What greater impiety could there be concerning Christ the Lord, that he should receive the law from a prophet as a mere man? But in our copy it reads מפמסנל [?] or in Hebrew letters מפומונאר [?], he shall receive the doctrine from the mouth of the Most High, as he himself said in John 7:16: My doctrine is not mine, but his who sent me. The letter י is often taken for י, and conversely, as in Hosea 9:16, where גוב stands for נוב; in the Venetian copy one finds זבאה [?], Job 5:7. In other copies I found כביא [?], and it is explained as from the mouth of the flourishing one their doctrine they shall worship. קבל means this, Genesis 8:21, and in Targum Jonathan on the first verse of this Psalm, where the Vulgate has The Lord said to my Lord, sit, etc. The Hebrew is נאם יהוה לארנישב [?], as if to say: the truth itself explains itself, Matthew 22:44; Luke 20:42; Acts 2:34. Re[?]

units.la: 34. Rabbini, ut secundam personam di-vinam sibi infensam argumentumq; cer-tissimum irrefragabile Domin. servato-ris dissolverent, ita corrumpunt Para-phrasin אמר יי במימריח dixit Domi-nus in verbo suo. Galat. lib. 8 cap. 24. se-quendo exemplaria correcta, ita legit אמר יהוה למימר יהתב לימיני dixit Deus verbo suo, sede ad dexteram meam ל pro כ fere semper pro eodem usurpan-tur, ut Prov. 2. 10. ילכך lego כלכך Thren. 1. 8. כמל comp. למל, in nostro vero exemplari. Syro [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters]?[illegible, ~6 letters] Hebraeis literis במי מריח ימיני אורך hoc est. Domino meo, He-roi suo seu possessori suo, dexteram mea, &c. in אמר יי, Dixit Dominus; omnes co-dices conveniunt; Syrus separatim legit Dictionem, כמי מריה, Rabbini conjun-ctim כמי מריה quod saepe fit, Isa. 1. 12. לאתרו שין Venet. תרו שין לא id est, ne conculcetis, & 19. vers. 10. שתי מחא Venet. שתי מחא, & 51. 19. ארנע יסתן Venet. ארנע יתתן, Jerem. 6. 25. & 12. in cap. 15. verf. 10. Sic inqvit Raphelengius in variis lectionibus ל ולמא Ven. rectius רשומה pro quo seperatim scribo מה רשי in Ezech. 27. 6. Osea 13. 14 Ju-dic. 5. 16. 1. Sam. 12, 6. & 19. 24. 2. Sam. 17. 2. & in qvamplurimis locis, hac separatione dictionum & mutatione literarum similium in similes, dolose totam Chaldaicam Paraphrasim vitiarunt impii Rabini; ita ut nullum pene sit testimonium a Christo Domino & ab Apostolis citatum in testamento novo: quod non sit adulteratum detortumque ad captivitatem; nec Prophetia de natali, passione, morte, resurrectione Domini, quæ non obcæcarent impietate Rabbinica, atquæ thalmundica fabula everterent; sicut præsepe Domini Adonidis simulacro, locum crucis Veneris statua, resurrectionis situm Jovis effigie obscurare conati sunt; sed quis contra Deum! Virtus tanta caligine obscurata refulget: ut Lucianus Θεὸς ἀπὸ μηχανῆς ἐπιφανείς. Virtuteque duce, comite fortuna: virtus enim eligit, quod est optimum. Quod si non succedit tamen in rebus præclaris,sicut in magnis etiam voluisse pulchrum est; sin succedit, ut mihi in inventione exemplarium prima laus debetur, virtuti tanquam egregii facinoris duci, proxima fortunæ,quæ virtuti subservierit. Jamjam Deo favente & duce, omnia loca adulterata à sacrilegis Rabbinis, demonstrant mysteria & Sacramenta magna Christi Domini legisque suæ Evangelicæ, ita ut suomet gladio interficiatur caput Goliath; & ne his immorer, universam Paraphrasim Chaldaicam veteris Testamenti ad primum candorem redactam & Latine redditam tradidit Paulo V. simulque, & N.T. textum Syriacum correctū, Latine quoque redditū cum Apocalypsi tribusque Epistolis &Historia adulteræ,quæ desidératur in Regiis Bibliis: Pontifex vero commisit hæc omnia Cardinali Bellarmino,qui convocavit Maronitarum Neophitarum Magistrum, correctrem Orientalium Linguarum, omnesque Rabbinos,Rabbenos,Morenos & sapientes, qui adhuc permanent in perfidia sua,ut recognoscerent exemplaria incorrupta,in veritateque acquiescerent, cui minime potuerunt adversari licet non pauci temporis spatium illis concessum fuerit, ut adverterent & notarent, si quid in textu Thargumico novarem, vel ipsius corruptor extitissem: sed nec minimum quidem invenientes, quod ad suæ infidelitatis scopum tenderet; & cum hoc minime à veritate Hebraica discrepat textus, nec à vulgata Latina Translatio ; quibus omnibus præviss & mature consideratis mihi facultas concessa ; fuit , ut typis mandaretur opus à me elaboratum: Pontifexque obtulit expensas, meoque nomine prodiret in lucem, dummodo non appellaretur Biblia Regia, sed Pontificia; adderetur qve textus Arabicus simul cum versione Latina : quod ego ardenter desiderabam. Nec precibus, gloria, nec utilitate motus in Hispaniam veni; tradidique opera Regi Philippo III. qui mihi designavit annuos reditus, & ad operis impressionem munificentissime expensas : sed morte Regis mens & voluntas, mutatur, magnus territat ossa sumptus, quo factum fuit, ut veniente Barberino Cardinali PonPontificis nepote, legatoqve ex latere ad Philippum IV. Regem, omnia hæc illi retuli, promisitqve mihi, si tradidissem opera, qvam primum ad urbem accederet, typis mandari: hac confidentia tradidi tomos Bibliæ Regiæ cum emendatione textus & versionis in margine notulis & numeris, & cum cæteris prædictis, qvæ desiderantur in Bibliis Regiis, qvæ omnia extant apud patrem generalem Religionis meæ: donec ego à Pontifice ad hoc opus vocatus Romam adeam; qvod exeqvi ægritudine & ætate confectus minime possum. Multa alia missa facio, ne Dominationem vestram delassem, cui persvadere atqve ad credendum ducere vellem, ne opus hoc incœptum proseqvatur; triumphabunt enim Judæi, & patebit eis aditus ad suam infidelitatem, nemini doctorum erit acceptum, Ecclesiæ scandalosum; si qvidem sub anathemate inditum ab ipso Pontifice, ne typis mandetur. Ego Dominationi vestræ spondeo infra breve tempus tradere omnia opera mea, hac conditione & lege, ut & nomine meo divulvulgentur,& ordinetur opus , sicut defignatum reperietur,& in pagina ista: elargitionem voluminum liberalitati & Magnificentiæ Dominationis vestræ relinquo. Vellem advertendum curet , versio-nem interlinearem Benedicti Ariæ Montani aliquos errores continere , quos notavi omnes v. 9. Psalmo 109. v. 4.
units.tr: 34. The rabbis, in order to dissolve the divine second person, who is hostile to them, and the most certain and irrefutable argument of the Lord Saviour, so corrupt the paraphrase: אמר יי במימריח [amar Yahweh bimeemrei], the Lord said in his word. Galatians, book 8, chapter 24. Following the corrected copies, it reads thus: אמר יהוה למימר יהתב לימיני [amar Yahweh lemeimar yehav limini], God said to his word, sit at my right hand. The letters ל and כ are almost always used for each other, as in Proverbs 2:10, where I read ילכך as כלכך; Lamentations 1:8, כמל for למל, which in our copy is ... [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters]?[illegible, ~6 letters] in Hebrew letters במי מריח ימיני אורך, that is: to my Lord, his Hero or his possessor, my right hand, etc. In אמר יי, the Lord said, all codices agree; the Syriac reads the word separately, כמי מריה, while the rabbis join it as כמי מריה, which often happens: Isaiah 1:12, לאתרו שין, Venetian תרו שין לא, that is, do not trample; and 19:10, שתי מחא, Venetian שתי מחא; and 51:19, ארנע יסתן, Venetian ארנע יתתן; Jeremiah 6:25 and 12; in chapter 15, verse 10. Thus Raphelengius in his Various Readings: ל ולמא, Venetian more correctly רשומה, for which I write separately מה רשי, in Ezekiel 27:6; Hosea 13:14; Judges 5:16; 1 Samuel 12:6 and 19:24; 2 Samuel 17:2, and in very many places. By this separation of words and change of similar letters into similar ones, the impious rabbis have craftily corrupted the whole Chaldee paraphrase, so that there is almost no testimony cited by Christ the Lord and the Apostles in the New Testament which has not been adulterated and twisted into captivity. Nor is there a prophecy of the birth, passion, death and resurrection of the Lord which they have not tried to blind by Rabbinic impiety, or overturn with Talmudic fable; just as they tried to obscure the manger of the Lord with the image of Adonis, the place of the cross with a statue of Venus, and the site of the resurrection with an effigy of Jove. But who can stand against God! Virtue, obscured by such darkness, shines forth, like the god who appears from the machine [Θεὸς ἀπὸ μηχανῆς ἐπιφανείς] in Lucian. With virtue as leader and fortune as companion: for virtue chooses what is best. If it does not succeed in noble undertakings, it is still fine to have wished for great things; but if it succeeds, as the first praise for the discovery of the copies is due to me, virtue being the leader of a splendid deed, the second praise is due to fortune, which has served virtue. Already now, with God favouring and leading, all the places corrupted by the sacrilegious rabbis reveal the mysteries and great sacraments of Christ the Lord and of his Evangelical law, so that the head of Goliath is slain by his own sword. And not to dwell on these things: I have handed to Paul V the whole Chaldee paraphrase of the Old Testament, restored to its first brightness and translated into Latin, and at the same time the Syriac text of the New Testament, corrected and also translated into Latin, together with the Apocalypse, three Epistles and the story of the adulteress, which is missing in the Royal Bibles. The Pope entrusted all these things to Cardinal Bellarmine, who summoned the master of the Maronite neophytes, the corrector of the Oriental languages, and all the rabbis, rabbis, Moors and wise men who still persist in their unbelief, that they might acknowledge the uncorrupted copies and acquiesce in the truth. They could scarcely oppose it, although they were granted a considerable span of time to notice and mark whether I had introduced anything new into the Targum text, or had myself been its corrupter. But finding not the least thing that tended to the goal of their unbelief, and since the text does not in any way differ from the Hebrew truth, nor the Latin translation from the Vulgate, after all these things had been weighed and carefully considered, I was granted leave to have the work I had prepared printed. The Pope offered the expenses, and it was to come out in my name, provided it was not called the Royal Bible but the Papal; and an Arabic text was to be added together with the Latin version, which I eagerly desired. Moved neither by entreaties, glory nor profit, I came to Spain and delivered my work to King Philip III, who assigned me an annual income and most generously the expenses for printing the work. But on the death of the King my mind and will changed, and the great cost frightened my bones. Hence it happened that when Cardinal Barberini, the Pope's nephew and legate a latere to King Philip IV, came, I reported all these things to him, and he promised me that, if I handed over the work, it would be printed as soon as he reached the city. On this confidence I handed over the volumes of the Royal Bible with the correction of text and version, with notes and numbers in the margin, and with the other things mentioned that are missing in the Royal Bibles; all of these are kept by the Father General of my Order, until I, called to this work by the Pope, go to Rome, which I am unable to do, worn out by sickness and age. I pass over many other things, lest I weary your Lordship, whom I wished to persuade and lead to believe that this work, once begun, should not be pursued; for the Jews will triumph, and an access will be opened for them to their unbelief; it will be unacceptable to none of the learned, and a scandal to the Church, since it was placed under anathema by the Pope himself, that it should not be printed. I promise your Lordship that within a short time I will hand over all my works, on this condition and law: that they be published under my name, and that the work be arranged as it is found designed on this page. The bestowal of the volumes I leave to the generosity and magnificence of your Lordship. I would like your Lordship to take care to note that the interlinear version of Benedictus Arias Montanus contains some errors, all of which I have marked: verse 9 of Psalm 109, verse 4 [of Psalm 110].

units.la: אתה כהן לעולם על דברתי מלכי־צדק
units.tr: You are a priest for ever, after the manner of Melchizedek [אתה כהן לעולם על דברתי מלכי־צדק]

units.la: Scilicet tu es sacerdos in seculum secundum morem Melchisedec. Arias ita vertit: super verbū meum,in quo non solùm ap-paret audacia temeraria in infringenda Apostoli explanatione ad Hebr. 7. ver.6. Secundum ordinem Melchisedec ; sed Lingvæ imperitia ; Jod enim est paragogicum ut dicimus,sicut vel sicuti, &c. inLingva Hebraica דברה & in regimine דברת mos seu ritus. Cur verò שאול in Psalmo 15. ver. 10. interpretatur sepulchrum,ut coincidat cum Hæreticis ; & in Psalmo 17. ver. 6, eandem infernum ex-ponit?ultro progredi minime valeo,quia male de corpore & animo. Parcat Dominatio sua mihi & ægro & afflicto : erroribus, quos confiteor plurimos, quia currenti calamo; paucissimum temporis spatium fuit mihi datum: responsum expecto, translationem Latinam Arabicam, ut accurate perlegam, si forte dissentiat à textu Arabico Hebraeo & à fide. Salve, Vale, Vive Madriti 29. Julii 1618.
units.tr: That is, you are a priest for ever according to the manner of Melchizedek. Arias translates it thus: according to my word, in which rendering there appears not only a rash audacity in overturning the Apostle's explanation at Heb. 7.6, after the order of Melchizedek, but also a lack of linguistic skill. For the Jod is paragogic, as we say sicut or sicuti, and so on. In Hebrew the word דברה, and in the construct form דברת, means mos seu ritus, that is, custom or manner. But why does he render שאול in Psalm 15.10 as sepulchrum, so that it agrees with the heretics, and in Psalm 17.6 expound the same word as infernum? I cannot go any further on my own, because I am unwell in body and in mind. May your Lordship spare me, sick and afflicted as I am. I confess that there are very many errors, since I wrote with a running pen and was given very little time. I await a reply, and the Latin translation of the Arabic, so that I may read it through carefully, in case it perhaps differs from the Arabic, the Hebrew text, or the faith. Farewell, be well, live. Madrid, 29 July 1618.

units.la: Andreas de Leon Zamorensis Clericorum regularium minor.
units.tr: Andreas de Leon of Zamora, a Minor among the regular clerks.

units.la: EPIST. IV.
units.tr: EPISTLE IV.

units.la: Joan. Morinus Clar. viro Hieronymo Aleandro de diversis Scripturae Samaritanae Characteribus, qui in diversis eorum libris reperiuntur.
units.tr: Joannes Morinus to the illustrious man Hieronymus Aleander, on the various characters of the Samaritan Scripture that are found in their different books.

units.la: Clarissimo & Doctissimo viro Hieronymo Aleandro Joannes Morinus S. D.
units.tr: To the most distinguished and learned man Hieronymus Aleander, Joannes Morinus sends greetings.

units.la: EOdem fere momento, quo mihi reddita est Epistola tua, allata mihi sunt exemplaria duodecim Praefationis, quam editioni Bibliorum Graecorum Sixti V. Pontificis Parisiis recens recusae praeposui; non plura curaveram extra ordinem numerumque Bibliopolis consvetum mihi exprimi, ut amicis nonnullis, qvibus editio Romana præsto est, illa communicarem: Epistolæ tuæ Præfationisq; meæ in manus meas eodem momento conversum velut omen accepi, quo fretus, eandem si tibi munusculi loco offerrem, non ingratam fore auguratus sum. Qvamqvam enim Præfationem istam te legere plurimum desiderarem, dubitabam tamen, an honestum satis & honorificum esset, fragmentum rebus aliis implicitum, majorisq; operis ἀποσπασμάτιον in exteras regiones ad virum mittere, quem maximi facio & facere debeo, sed dubitationem animo eximit inopinatus ille eventus, statimqve in mentem venit, amicos amicitiæ delicta facile condonare; de istius Præfationis scopo non plura, ipse sese explicat; addam tamen de Samaritanorum Pentateucho, qvi penes nos est, nonnulla me inserere: cum autem illum evolverem, characteresqve Pentateuchi istius cum characteribus, quos in lucem ediderunt vel Scaliger vel Villalpandus, compararem, quamquam characteres eosdem esse facile judicarem, in omnibus tamen fere dissimilitudinem aliquam deprehendi, sed multo majorem in libello quodam Romae recens Italice excuso, quem ante paucos dies raptim legi. Sed literam Tau de qua in opusculo tuo docte disputas, hac semper forma [illegible, ~1 letters] in eo Codice effictam video, quae parum ad crueem mihi pertinere videtur. Unum vir doctissime, te plurimum rogatum velim, idmodo tibi non sit oneri futurum, ut cum otio abundabis, inscriptiones Siclorum, de quibus mentionem facis, iisdem, quibus scripti sunt, characteribus exscribicures, & ad me mittere non graveris: editionem Pentateuchi Samaritani jussu Illustrissimi Cardinalis Berulli meditor; inscriptiones ejusmodi coeptum meum plurimum adjuvabunt: Preces meae parum civiles, ne temerarias dicam, videri possunt, qui adeo repetita amicitia tua abutar; sed eas ut spero, facile excusabunt & tuum in litteras studium, & tua in me humanitas.
units.tr: At almost the same moment that your letter was delivered to me, twelve copies of the Preface were brought to me, which I placed before the Parisian reprint of the Greek Bible of Pope Sixtus V. I had not arranged for more copies than the booksellers usually print to be struck off outside the ordinary number, so that I could share them with some friends who already have the Roman edition. As soon as I received your letter and my Preface, I took it as a kind of omen that they reached my hands at the same moment, and I judged that if I offered you this little gift, it would not be unwelcome. For although I very much wished you to read that Preface, I hesitated whether it was proper and respectful to send a fragment, bound up with other matters and a mere extract from a larger work, to a man abroad whom I hold in the highest esteem and ought to hold in that esteem. But that unexpected occurrence removes my doubt, and it comes to mind that friends readily pardon the faults of friendship. As for the purpose of that Preface, I say no more, since it explains itself. I will add, however, a few remarks on the Samaritan Pentateuch that is in our possession. When I unrolled it and compared its characters with those that Scaliger or Villalpandus published, I easily judged that the characters were the same, yet I found some dissimilarity in nearly all of them, and a much greater one in a small book recently printed in Italian at Rome, which I read hastily a few days ago. But the letter Tau, about which you learnedly discuss in your little work, I see is always shaped in that manuscript in a form [illegible, about one letter], which seems to me to have little to do with the cross. There is one thing, most learned sir, that I would ask you very earnestly: if it will not be a burden to you, when you have leisure in abundance, please copy out the inscriptions of the shekels you mention in the very characters in which they were written, and do not hesitate to send them to me. I am planning an edition of the Samaritan Pentateuch at the command of the most illustrious Cardinal Berulle, and inscriptions of this kind will greatly help my undertaking. My requests may seem rather uncivil, not to say rash, since I am abusing your renewed friendship in this way; but I hope that your zeal for letters and your kindness toward me will readily excuse them.

units.la: EPIST. V.
units.tr: EPIST. V.

units.la: Hier. Aleander viro Doct. J. Morino de variis exemplaribus, nec non Charact- eribus Samaritanorum.
units.tr: Hieronymus Aleander to the learned J. Morinus, on various manuscripts, and also on the characters of the Samaritans.

units.la: Viro Doctissimo & Religiosissimo Jo. Morino, Hier. Aleander S. D.
units.tr: To the most learned and most devout Jo. Morinus, Hieronymus Aleander sends greetings.

units.la: SErius qvidem tuæ ad me literæ pervenerunt pridie idus Martias datæ, qvippe illas superiore tantum hebdomada accepi; verùm adeo jucundæ fuerunt, ut nihil accidere mihi jucundius optatiusqve posset; cum præter non obscura tui in me amoris indicia, doctissimam Præsationem afferrent in novam istam veteris Testamenti à LXX. translati editionem:qva sane Præfatione nihil eruditius, accuratius nihil concinnari poterat. Eam ego statim devoravi, non legi, adeo hujusmodi epularum sum avidus; ac tam svavi sacræ doctrinæ, ut ita loqvar, lucco imbutum me sensi, ut mirifica qvadam voluptate totus sim perfusus. Qvamobrem, qvod participem hujusce dissertationis facere me volueris, valde te amo, ac debere me tibi plurimum fa-teor; quod scribis Illustrissimum Card. Berullum de edendo Pentateucho Samaritanis literis exarato cogitare, id mihi consilii vehementer probatur, tantoque Antistite Doctissimo nimirum & Christianæ pietatis inprimis studioso dignum videtur. Ac scias velim, esse hic quoque in Vaticana Bibliotheca aliud Pentateuchi exemplar, iisdem Samaritanis litteris scriptum, quod quinque abhinc annis piæ memoriæ Scipio Cardinalis S. Susannæ tunc Bibliothecarius CCC. aureorum pretio comparavit, atque is quidem codex, etsi Characteres habet Samaritanos, Hebraica tamen Lingua, uti & vestrum, confectum est. At vero Petrus à Valle patricius Romanus, qui duodecim totos annos in Orientalibus regionibus consumpsit, & cujus potissimum opera ut audio, pater Harleus Sancius codicem istum suum nactus est, aliud Pentateuchi exemplar Romam detulit, quod non charactere tantum sed & idiomate Samaritano conscriptum est. Ac rem me tibi gratam facturum existimavi, si primam periodum ex eo codice descriptam ad te mitterem, quam habebis in schedula huic Epistolæ addita: si qva vero in re hi characteres ab iis forsitan, qvi vestro in codice leguntur, variantes erunt, ubi & mihi significaveris, horum ego Alphabetum conficiam, &, si tanti erit, istuc transmittam. Interim delineationesqvorundam siclorum accipies, & alias postmodum tibi curabo; nam plures nunc qvidem perqvirere per temporis angustiam non licuit: tu nostra, ut lubet & qvoties lubet, opera utere, nihil enim facere gratius mihi potes.
units.tr: Your letter, dated the day before the Ides of March, reached me rather late, for I received it only a week ago. Yet it was so pleasing that nothing could have given me greater delight. Besides the clear signs of your affection for me, it brought your most learned preface to the new edition of the Old Testament translated by the Seventy. Nothing could have been more learned or more carefully put together than that preface. I devoured it at once, I did not merely read it, so eager am I for such feasts. I felt that I had been steeped in, so to speak, the sweet juice of sacred learning, and I was wholly suffused with a wonderful pleasure. So I love you greatly for wishing to make me a sharer in this discourse, and I confess that I owe you a great deal. As for your report that the most illustrious Cardinal Barberini is thinking of publishing a Pentateuch written in Samaritan letters, I heartily approve of the plan, and it seems fitting for so great a prelate, most learned and above all devoted to Christian piety. I should also like you to know that here in the Vatican Library there is another copy of the Pentateuch, written in the same Samaritan letters. Five years ago Cardinal Scipio of S. Susanna, then librarian, of blessed memory, bought it for three hundred gold pieces. This codex, although it has Samaritan characters, is nevertheless composed in the Hebrew language, as is your copy. But Pietro della Valle, a Roman patrician, who spent a full twelve years in the Eastern lands, and through whose effort, as I hear, Father Harleus Sancius obtained his own codex, brought to Rome another copy of the Pentateuch, written not only in Samaritan characters but also in the Samaritan idiom. I thought I would do you a favour by sending you the first sentence copied from that codex, which you will find on a slip added to this letter. If these characters perhaps differ in some respects from those read in your codex, please let me know, and I will prepare an alphabet of them and, if it is worth the trouble, send it to you there. Meanwhile you will receive drawings of some shekels, and I will see to others later, for the shortness of time did not allow me to seek out more at present. Make use of my services as you wish and as often as you wish, for you can do nothing more pleasing to me.

units.la: Vale, Romæ, Kalendis Maii MDCXXVIII.
units.tr: Farewell. From Rome, on the Kalends of May, 1628.

units.la: EPIST. VI.
units.tr: LETTER VI.

units.la: Hier. Aleander eidem de siclis quibus- dam Samaritano Charactere exaratis, forma Literæ Tau apud Samaritanos.
units.tr: Girolamo Aleandro to the same man, concerning certain shekels inscribed with Samaritan characters, and the shape of the letter Tau among the Samaritans.

units.la: Jo. Morino viro Doctissimo Hieronymus Aleander S. D.
units.tr: To Jean Morin, most learned of men, Girolamo Aleandro sends greetings.

units.la: MIsi ad te superioribus septimanis trium siclorum delineationes, reqve[?] de duobus Pentateuchi Samaritani exemplaribus, quæ hic habemus, feci certiorem: ac lætabor sane, meam tibi diligentiam non infructuosam fuisse, saltem non injucundam. Duos hic præterea siclos reperi, alterum ex recentioribus, iis nimirum, quos Scaliger viderat, qui propterea pronunciare ausus est, non alios Characteres siclis inesse, quam quibus hodie Hebræi utuntur; alterum longe minorem, qui asservatur in Musæo Francisci Gvaldi equitis Ariminensis, in quo Characteres sunt antiquiores, illi videlicet, quos Samaritani retinerunt, sed adeo detriti, ut nullum inde verbum exculpi possit: ne quid tamen in me diligentiæ desiderares,& hunc delineandum curavi. Perspicies in utraque nummi facie litteram Tau in similitudinem crucis effictam, & mirum sane videri potest, quod cum antiquitus hoc modo scriberetur X posterioribus temporibus in eam N[?]degeneravit: verum scribendi celeritatem in causa fuisse existimo, ut enim unico ductu calami efformaretur ita vi-detur detur exarari cœpta )-( N qvemadmodum nos literam Romanam X cursim hodie scribentes sic pingere solemus )-( ex quo postea orta recentior illa Samaritana N: qvicqvid sit, mirum non est, Characterum figuras tractu temporis subinde variari. Si qvis posthac siclus ad manus venerit meas, non committam, qvo minus ejus statim delineationem ac-cipias.
units.tr: In recent weeks I informed you, by letter, of the drawings of three shekels, and of the two copies of the Samaritan Pentateuch that we have here. I am certainly glad that my diligence was not without fruit for you, or at least was not unwelcome. Here I have also found two shekels. One is of more recent date, of the kind Scaliger had seen, which is why he ventured to declare that the shekels bear no characters other than those the Hebrews use today. The other is much smaller and is kept in the museum of Francesco Gualdo, knight of Rimini. Its characters are older, namely those the Samaritans have retained, but they are so worn that no word can be made out from them. Still, lest you should find any lack of diligence in me, I have had this one drawn as well. In both faces of the coin you will see the letter Tau, formed in the likeness of a cross. It may seem strange indeed that, although it was written this way in ancient times, it later degenerated into N. I think the cause was the speed of writing. For as it was formed with a single stroke of the pen, so it seems to have begun to be written as )-( N, just as we Romans nowadays, writing the letter X in haste, are accustomed to draw it as )-(. From this the more recent Samaritan N later arose. Whatever the case, it is no wonder that the shapes of the characters vary over time. If any shekel comes into my hands hereafter, I will not hold back from sending you its drawing at once.

units.la: Vale. Romæ. Die penult. Maij 1628.
units.tr: Farewell. Rome, the penultimate day of May, 1628.

units.la: EPIST. VII,
units.tr: EPIST. VII,

units.la: Hier. Aleander eidem de aliis Siclis Sa- maritanorum, simulqve de Pentateu- cho Samarit.
units.tr: Hieronymus Aleander to the same man, concerning the other shekels of the Samaritans, and also concerning the Samaritan Pentateuch.

units.la: Doctissimo viro Jo. Morino Hier. Alean-der S.
units.tr: To the most learned man Jo. Morinus, Hier. Aleander, greetings.

units.la: NOn injucundum tibi fuisse operam meam, ex tuis literis perspexi a.d.IV. Nonas Junii datis. Jam vero meas alteras ad te pervenisse censeo, quibus duorum siclorum delineationes addideram: alium nuper siclum reperi in cimeliis Illustrissimi Card. Barberini, cujus itidem typum ad te mittere volui, tametsi Cha-racteres habeat aliqva ex parte jam vetustate detritos ac fugientes. Rogavi etiam per litteras humanissimum doctissimum-qve Perium Dominum Senatorem Sextiaaqvensem,ut suorum tibi siclorum copiam faceret; & qvoniam vir est juvandis literis natus, non dubito, qvin anteqvam prælo committatur vestri istius Pentateuchi exemplar,ejus tu humanitatis experimentum sis visurus. Petro etiam à Valle persvadere conatus sum, ut Samariticum suum Pentateuchum edi patiatur, nec sane hominem ab hujusmodi editione abhorrere video, dummodo ne suo hoc exemplari careat; opus autem esset, Lingvam illam Samariticam aliqvis addisceret,ut Librum Latini posset reddere: qvod ei arduum non fore existimo, qvi cum Hebraico idiomate Chaldaicum ac Syriacum calleat. Tu de re tota cogitabis, si consilium secutus Illustrissimi Cardinalis Berulli,in ea sentntia persistis, ut vestrum istud lucem videat,idqve è re Christiana esse cognoscis. Pulcherima certe visa mihi sunt, quæ tu ex collatione Samaritici Pentateuchi cum Hebraico observasti; & sane auctor tibi sum, ut qua diligentia facis, de Religione, deque litteris bene mereri pergas.
units.tr: I have learned from your letter, dated the fourth day before the Nones of June, that my work was not unwelcome to you. I now think my second letter has reached you, in which I had added drawings of two shekels. Lately I have found another shekel among the treasures of the most illustrious Cardinal Barberini, and I wished to send you its impression as well, although its characters are in part already worn away by age and hard to make out. I also asked by letter the most kind and learned Peiresc, senator of Aix, to give you a supply of his shekels. Since he is a man born to help scholarship, I do not doubt that before your edition of the Pentateuch goes to press you will experience his kindness. I have also tried to persuade Pietro della Valle to allow his Samaritan Pentateuch to be published. I see that the man does not shrink from such an edition, provided he is not deprived of his own copy. Someone would, however, have to learn that Samaritan language so as to render the book into Latin, and I do not think this would be hard for one who knows Chaldee and Syriac as well as Hebrew. As for the whole matter, you will think it over, if, following the counsel of the most illustrious Cardinal Bérulle, you persist in the view that your work should see the light, and you recognize that this serves the Christian cause. Certainly the observations you made from comparing the Samaritan Pentateuch with the Hebrew seem to me most excellent. Indeed, I advise you to continue to deserve well of religion and of letters with the same diligence you now show.

units.la: Vale. Romæ die XIII. Julii M. DC XXVIII.
units.tr: Farewell. Rome, 13 July 1628.

units.la: EPIST. VIII.
units.tr: Letter VIII.

units.la: Jo. Morinus Hier. Aleandro de eodem Argumento.
units.tr: Joannes Morinus to Hieronymus Aleander, on the same subject.

units.la: Clarissimo & Doctissimo viro Hier. Aleandro Joan. Morinus. S. D.
units.tr: To the most distinguished and learned man Hieronymus Aleander, from Joannes Morinus, greetings.

units.la: MIssæ sunt ad me Parisiis Lugdunum, quò Lugdunensem Archiepiscopum, qui nunc obiit, comitatus eram, binæ litteræ tuæ, utraque benevolentiæ ergame tuæ signa secum deferentes, priores duorum siclorum ἔντυπα, unius vero posteriores; lætitia sane non modica perfusus sum, cum coepta mea precesq; adeo cordi tibi fuisse animadverti, ut de iis juvandis tam sæpe cogitares: rem fecisti mihi gratissimam, quæqve me tibi arctissimò devinctum tenet. Paulo maturius litteris tuis respondissem, nisi Lugduno statim Lutetiam mihi redeundum fuisset, nunc autem improvisis negotiis occupatus raptim scribo, quod libere & amice hoc audeam, non indignaberis: Argenteus siclus Illustrissimi Cardinalis[?] Barberini plane genuinus est & syncerus, literæ quædam obliteratæ sunt, sed delineationes superstites, quæ desunt facile demonstrant. In una facie hæc est inscriptio Latine reddita, Hierusalem sancta; in altera ,siclus; deinde litera quæ ad He, proxime accedit, cæteræ deletæ sunt: alius siclus apud Ludovicum Aubery adulterinus est, Characteres non sunt Samaritici, sed vulgares Hebræi, quaes[?] fere cudebantur ante 8o. aut 1oo.[?] annos, si litteram Coph excipias quæ paulo diversa forma sculpitur. Inscriptionis idem sensus qui aliorum nonnullorum Hierusalem sancta, ex una parte, ex altera siclus Israel. De alio siclo qui apud Franciscum Gualdum, nondum judicare possum, Characteres enim, ut probe notasti, admodum detriti sunt. Habeo tibi gratias maximas, qvod literis tuis apud Doctissimum & Ampliss. servatorem Peresium in mei gratiam intercedere voluisti, eandem gratiam ab aliis amicis pariter impetrabo. Plurimum præterea gaudeo, qvòd clarissimus Petrus à Valle Pentateuchum suum publicæ utilitati non invideat; si concedere vellet, ut Geneseos liber vel saltem nonnulla capita exscriberentur, eaqve ad me mitterentur, de me plurimum mereretur. Reverendus Pater Bertinus noster Amanuensium sumptibus satisfaciet; descriptio autem fieri oportet, qva ejusmodi lineæ ἐκτύπῳ lineis πρω-τοτύπῳ paginæ paginis æqvo numero responderent, ut si qvod discrimen in describo excidat, facilius deprehenderetur: de Lingva Samaritica intelligenda parum laboro; cùm enim Chaldaica sit, & Pentateuchus Hebræus Characteribus Samaritics [?] descriptus, alterius sit interpretatio non admodum difficili negotio: conjicio Dialecti istius etiam minutias qvasqve consequar. Vale, vir Ciarissime [?], & de me bene mereri perge.
units.tr: Two letters from you reached me at Paris, and I received them at Lyon, where I had gone with the Archbishop of Lyon, who has now died. Both carried signs of your goodwill towards me. The first enclosed two shekels as impressions [ἔντυπα], and the second one. I was truly not a little delighted to learn that my undertakings and my prayers were so dear to you that you thought so often about helping them. You have done me a most welcome favour, and it binds me very closely to you. I would have replied to your letters somewhat sooner, but I had to return from Lyon straight to Lutetia, and now, busy with unexpected business, I write in haste. You will not be offended that I dare to say this frankly and as a friend. The silver shekel of the most illustrious Cardinal Barberini is entirely genuine and unadulterated. Some letters have been rubbed away, but the surviving outlines easily show what is missing. On one face is the inscription, given in Latin, Holy Jerusalem; on the other ,shekel; then a letter that comes close to He, and the rest are effaced. Another shekel, the one owned by Louis Aubery, is counterfeit. Its characters are not Samaritan but ordinary Hebrew, the kind that were minted about eighty or a hundred years ago, except for the letter Qoph, which is cut in a slightly different form. The inscription has the same sense as some others: on one side Holy Jerusalem, on the other shekel of Israel. I cannot yet judge the other shekel that belongs to François Gualdo, since, as you rightly noted, its characters are very worn. I owe you my greatest thanks for being willing to intercede on my behalf with the most learned and most honourable keeper, Peiresc, through your letters. I will likewise obtain the same favour from my other friends. I am also very glad that the most distinguished Pietro della Valle does not begrudge his Pentateuch to the public good. If he were willing to allow the book of Genesis, or at least some chapters of it, to be copied out and sent to me, he would earn my deepest gratitude. Our Reverend Father Bertinus will meet the cost of the scribes. The copying must be done so that the lines of the copy correspond to the lines of the original [πρωτοτύπῳ] page by page, in the same number, so that if any discrepancy slips in during the transcription, it can be detected more easily. I am not taking much trouble over understanding the Samaritan language. Since it is Chaldean, and the Hebrew Pentateuch is written in Samaritan characters, its interpretation is not a very difficult task. I suppose that I shall also grasp the finer points of that dialect. Farewell, most distinguished man, and continue to deserve well of me.

units.la: EPIST. IX.
units.tr: Letter IX
